A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 반 티셔츠 디자인으로 가장 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Emma, is that the design for our class T-shirt?
W: Yes. We'll wear it on sports day. Look, there's a lion on the front.
M: Cool. Is our class number under the lion?
W: No, it's on the back. And the T-shirt is yellow.
M: Yellow? I thought we chose white.
W: We did, but white gets dirty too fast.
choices: 흰 티셔츠 앞면에 사자가 있고, 반 번호는 뒷면에 있는 디자인
노란 티셔츠 앞면에 사자가 있고, 반 번호는 뒷면에 있는 디자인
노란 티셔츠 앞면에 사자가 있고, 그 아래에 반 번호가 있는 디자인
노란 티셔츠 앞면에 별이 있고, 반 번호는 뒷면에 있는 디자인
A.explain_ko: 앞면에 사자, 반 번호는 뒷면, 색은 흰색에서 노란색으로 바뀌었다. 흰색·사자 아래 번호는 대화에서 나왔다가 아니라고 한 것이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 관계로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Hello. Are you here for a family photo?
W: Yes. It's for my grandma's seventieth birthday.
M: Great. Please sit here, and your brother can stand behind you.
W: Like this? Should I take off my glasses?
M: No, they look nice. Now, everyone, look at the camera and smile.
W: Did my brother close his eyes?
M: Yes, he did. Let's take one more.
A.explain_ko: 가족사진을 찍으러 온 손님에게 자리를 잡아 주고 카메라를 보라고 하므로 사진사와 손님이다. 안경·할머니는 대화에 나온 말로 만든 오답이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 심정으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Tom, you look down. What's wrong?
M: My family was going to go fishing at the river this Saturday, but my dad has to work.
W: Oh, that's too bad. You were looking forward to it.
M: Yes. I wanted to catch a really big fish this time.
W: Maybe you can go next weekend.
M: Wait, my dad just sent me a message. He doesn't have to work after all!
W: Really? So you can go?
M: Yes! And my uncle is bringing his boat. I can't wait!
A.explain_ko: 처음에는 낚시를 못 가서 실망했지만, 아빠가 일하지 않아도 된다는 소식에 삼촌 배까지 타게 되어 마지막에는 신이 났다. '실망한'은 처음 심정이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 남자에게 부탁한 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Sam, the students from Canada are visiting our school this Friday.
M: I know. Our class is having a welcome party for them, right?
W: Yes. Emily is drawing a big welcome sign, and Mr. Hall will bring snacks.
M: What about name tags?
W: Jason and I are making them tonight. But we still need someone to take photos at the party.
M: I have a good camera at home.
W: Great. Can you do it for us? We want to make a photo book for them.
M: Sure. I'll bring my camera on Friday.
A.explain_ko: 여자는 파티에서 사진 찍을 사람이 필요하다며 카메라가 있는 남자에게 부탁했다. 표지판은 Emily, 간식은 Mr. Hall, 이름표는 여자와 Jason이 맡았다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Dad, I'm going to bake banana bread for Grandpa's visit tomorrow.
M: Sounds great, Olivia. Do you have a recipe?
W: Yes, but I want to make it my own way. I'll use honey instead of sugar and add some chocolate chips.
M: Is this your first time making banana bread?
W: Yes. Why?
M: When you try a recipe for the first time, I think you should follow it exactly. Then you'll know how it's supposed to taste. If you change many things at once and the bread fails, you won't know what went wrong. Next time, you can change one thing and see the difference.
W: Okay. I'll use sugar this time.
choices: 설탕 대신 꿀을 넣으면 더 건강한 빵을 만들 수 있다.
처음 만드는 요리는 요리법을 그대로 따라 해야 한다.
손님이 오는 날에는 처음 해 보는 요리를 하지 않는 것이 좋다.
요리를 잘하려면 여러 재료를 한꺼번에 바꿔 보아야 한다.
A.explain_ko: 아빠는 처음 해 보는 요리법은 그대로 따라 해야 맛이 어때야 하는지 알고, 한꺼번에 여러 가지를 바꾸면 무엇이 잘못됐는지 모른다고 한다. 꿀·설탕, 할아버지 방문은 대화에 나온 말로 만든 오답이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Excuse me. Do you have these hiking boots in size nine?
W: Let me check our stock. I'm sorry, but size nine is sold out in brown.
M: Oh no. My family is going hiking in the mountains this week. I really need new boots.
W: I can order a pair for you. They'll arrive on Friday.
M: Friday is too late. We're leaving on Wednesday morning.
W: I see. Well, we have the same boots in size nine, but in gray. Would you like to try them on?
choices: Great. I'll pick them up on Friday, then.
No problem. I'll wait until the brown ones arrive.
Sure. The color isn't important to me.
Thanks, but size nine is too big for me.
A.explain_ko: 갈색은 금요일에나 오는데 수요일에 떠나야 하므로, 같은 치수의 회색을 신어 보겠다는 응답이 알맞다. 금요일에 찾으러 오겠다는 말은 떠나는 날 뒤라 맞지 않는다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 전화한 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Hello, Brush and Color Art Studio. This is Mark speaking.
W: Hi, Mark. This is Karen Wells. My son Tyler takes your watercolor class on Tuesdays.
M: Oh, yes. Tyler is doing really well. His painting of the harbor last week was wonderful.
W: Thank you. He loves your class. Actually, that's why I'm calling. Starting next month, he has swimming practice on Tuesdays, but he doesn't want to give up painting.
M: I see. We have the same watercolor class on Thursdays at four thirty.
W: That would be perfect. Is there any space in that class?
M: Yes, there are two spots left. Should I move him to Thursdays from next month?
W: Yes, please. And does he need to bring anything new?
M: No, the same brushes and paper will be fine.
choices: 아들의 그림을 칭찬해 준 것에 감사하려고
A.explain_ko: 화요일에 수영 연습이 생겨 아들의 수채화 수업을 목요일로 옮기려고 전화했다. 칭찬·수영·준비물은 대화 중에 곁들여 나온 이야기다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Hi. I'd like to buy some souvenirs for my friends back home.
M: Sure. These keychains are very popular. They're five dollars each.
W: They're cute. I'll take four. And how much is this mug with the lighthouse on it?
M: It's fifteen dollars. If you buy two mugs, the second one is half price.
W: I only need one. It's for my aunt.
M: Okay. Anything else?
W: What about these postcards?
M: They're one dollar each, but they're free if you spend thirty dollars or more.
W: Great. Then I'll take three postcards, too. Oh, wait. My friend Jake already has a keychain like this. I'll take three keychains, not four.
M: No problem. So, three keychains, one mug, and three postcards.
W: That's right. Here's my card.
A.explain_ko: 열쇠고리 3개 $15 + 머그 1개 $15 = $30이고, $30 이상이라 엽서 3장은 무료다. $35는 열쇠고리 4개로 계산한 값, $33은 엽서 값을 더한 값이다.

A.question: 다음을 듣고, 학교 앨범 사진 촬영에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
A.script: M: Hello, everyone. This is Nathan Hughes, your student council president. I'd like to tell you about Yearbook Photo Day. Photos for this year's yearbook will be taken next Tuesday and Wednesday in the school auditorium. First-year students will have their photos taken on Tuesday, and second- and third-year students will have theirs taken on Wednesday. Please wear your school uniform, and don't forget your name tag. Each photo takes only about two minutes, so your homeroom teacher will send you there in small groups during class time. If you are absent on your day, you can come to the make-up session next Monday after school. Also, the photographers will take a group photo of every club on Thursday at lunchtime. Club leaders should sign up at the student council room by this Friday. Thank you.
choices: 동아리 단체 사진은 목요일 방과 후에 찍는다.
결석한 학생은 다음 주 월요일 방과 후에 찍을 수 있다.
A.explain_ko: 동아리 단체 사진은 목요일 점심시간에 찍는다. '방과 후'는 결석자 보충 촬영(월요일)에 나온 말이다.

A.question:
다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 예약할 고래 관찰 투어를 고르시오.
투어 | 출발 시각 | 걸리는 시간 | 1인 가격 | 점심
A | 8:00 | 3시간 | $45 | 없음
B | 9:30 | 4시간 | $60 | 있음
C | 10:00 | 2시간 | $40 | 없음
D | 1:00 (오후) | 4시간 | $55 | 있음
A.script:
W: Honey, let's book a whale-watching tour for the last day of our trip. Here are four tours.
M: Great. The kids will love it. Look, the eight o'clock tour is cheap.
W: Eight? Remember how hard it was to wake the kids up yesterday? I don't think we can make it.
M: You're right. Then how about the ten o'clock one? It's the cheapest of all.
W: But it's only two hours long. The hotel staff told me the whales usually stay far from the shore, so we need at least three hours.
M: Okay. Then we have two choices left. The nine thirty tour includes lunch.
W: It does, but it costs too much. We said we'd spend no more than fifty-five dollars per person.
M: Then this one is perfect. It includes lunch, too.
W: Good. Let's book it now.
A.explain_ko: 8시 출발(A)은 아이들이 못 일어나서, 2시간짜리(C)는 너무 짧아서, 1인 $60(B)은 예산 $55를 넘어서 빠진다. 남는 것은 D다.

A.question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script: W: Hello, listeners. This is Rebecca Stone with Family on the Road. When parents plan a family vacation, they usually decide everything themselves: where to stay, what to see, and where to eat. Then they wonder why their children look bored in the back seat. Here's my suggestion. Give each child one part of the trip to plan. A ten-year-old can choose the restaurant for one dinner. A teenager can research a museum and decide which rooms the family will visit first. Of course, you can set a budget and a few simple rules. But once the choice is made, try to follow it, even if it isn't what you would pick. Children who plan part of a trip pay more attention, ask more questions, and remember the places much longer. Their small decisions turn them from passengers into real travelers. So on your next vacation, share the map.
choices: 가족 여행의 예산과 규칙은 부모가 미리 정해 두어야 한다.
자녀와 여행할 때는 박물관처럼 배울 것이 많은 곳을 골라야 한다.
여행 일정은 여유 있게 짜서 자녀가 지루하지 않게 해야 한다.
가족 여행 계획의 일부를 자녀에게 맡기면 자녀가 여행에 더 깊이 참여한다.
A.explain_ko: 아이마다 여행의 한 부분을 계획하게 하면 더 집중하고 오래 기억한다는 것이 요지다. 예산·규칙, 박물관은 예로 든 세부 내용이다.

A.question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Grace가 Owen에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script: W: Grace and her classmate Owen meet every Saturday at a café near their school to study for their chemistry exam. They usually study there from ten until two. The café used to be quiet, but last month a music class started next door, and now it gets very noisy after eleven. Owen suggests moving to the city library, but Grace knows that all of the library's study rooms are booked for the whole month. Then she remembers that her aunt's bakery is closed on Saturdays, and there is a large table in the back room. She calls her aunt, and her aunt says they are welcome to use it. So Grace wants to suggest to Owen that they study at the bakery from next Saturday. In this situation, what would Grace most likely say to Owen?
choices: How about studying in the back room of my aunt's bakery from next week?
Why don't we book a study room at the city library?
Let's come to the café earlier, before the music class starts.
Could you ask the music teacher to keep the noise down?

A.passage: Every day, at the same times, weather stations around the world send big balloons high into the sky. These weather balloons are filled with a gas that is lighter than air, so they rise quickly. Each balloon carries a small box with tools inside. As it goes up, the box measures the temperature and how wet the air is. Then it sends this information back to the ground. The air gets thinner higher up, so the balloon slowly grows bigger. A.question: 이것은 50년 전에 지어진 다리이다. (bridge, build, years, ago)

A.question: 위에서 보면, 그 섬은 하트처럼 보인다. (see, above, island, look, heart)

A.question: 그 상자가 너무 무거워서 들 수 없으면, 우리는 아빠께 도움을 청할 것이다. (box, heavy, lift, ask, Dad, help)

B.question: [catch] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.

B.question: [health] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.

B.explain_ko: keep + 목적어 + 형용사(목적격 보어). 명사 health → 형용사 healthy

B.question: [who] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.

B.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대 → If + had + 과거분사(brought), would have + 과거분사

B.question: [do] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.

B.question: 열쇠가 없어서, 나는 집 밖에서 기다렸다. (not, have, key, wait, outside, house)

B.question: 수영할 수 있을 만큼 날씨가 따뜻하면, 우리는 해변에 갈 것이다. (it, warm, enough, to, swim, go, beach)

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __borrow__
A.explain_ko: borrow는 '빌리다'. '빌려주다'는 lend, '돌려주다'는 return.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __careful__
A.explain_ko: careful은 '조심하는'. 부주의한은 careless, 걱정하는은 worried.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __일기__
A.explain_ko: 일기는 diary. dairy는 '유제품', dial은 '다이얼'로 철자가 비슷한 오답.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __prepare__
A.explain_ko: prepare는 '준비하다'. 비교하다는 compare, 보호하다는 protect.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __ancient__
A.explain_ko: ancient는 '고대의, 아주 오래된'. 현대의는 modern, 외국의는 foreign.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __습관__

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __consume__
A.explain_ko: consume은 '소비하다'. 생산하다는 produce, 보존하다는 preserve.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __valuable__
A.explain_ko: valuable은 '귀중한, 값비싼'. 편리한은 convenient, 가능한은 possible.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __실험__
A.explain_ko: 실험은 experiment. experience는 '경험', expert는 '전문가'로 같은 ex-로 시작하는 오답.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __evaluate__
A.explain_ko: evaluate는 '평가하다'. 증명하다는 prove, 전달하다는 deliver.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __frequent__
A.explain_ko: frequent는 '빈번한, 잦은'. 드문은 rare, 정확한은 accurate.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __의무__
A.explain_ko: 의무는 obligation. observation은 '관찰', operation은 '수술, 작동'으로 어미가 같은 오답.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __undermine__
A.explain_ko: undermine은 '(서서히) 약화시키다'. 강조하다는 emphasize, 보장하다는 guarantee.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __ambiguous__
A.explain_ko: ambiguous는 '애매모호한'. '야심 찬'은 철자가 비슷한 ambitious, '명백한'은 obvious.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __편견__
A.explain_ko: 편견은 prejudice. precedent는 '선례', premise는 '전제'로 같은 pre-로 시작하는 오답.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

A.explain_ko: yesterday가 있어 과거, 주어 Mina는 3인칭 단수이고 뒤에 형용사 tired가 오므로 be동사 was.

A.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?

Don't run in the hallway during the break.
Does your uncle work at the train station?
My little brother can swims very well in the sea.
Be careful with the hot pan on the stove.
A.explain_ko: 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형이 오므로 can swims가 아니라 can swim. 나머지는 3인칭 단수·의문문·명령문이 바르다.

A.question: 다음 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
A.passage:
Jake finished (A) _____ his room an hour ago.
He decided (B) _____ the soccer team next year.
A.explain_ko: finish는 동명사를 목적어로(cleaning), decide는 to부정사를 목적어로(to join) 쓴다.

A.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
A.passage:
a. This cake tastes sweetly.
b. I have visited the science museum twice.
c. The bridge was built in 1990.
d. She has lost her phone yesterday.
e. This blanket feels soft.
A.explain_ko: b·c·e가 맞다. a는 감각동사 taste 뒤에 형용사 sweet, d는 yesterday와 현재완료를 함께 쓸 수 없어 lost가 되어야 한다.

A.question: 다음 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
A.passage:
(A) _____ I need now is a cup of hot tea.
Look at the boy (B) _____ a kite by the river.
A.explain_ko: (A)는 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 What(~하는 것), (B)는 '연을 날리고 있는' 능동의 뜻이므로 현재분사 flying.

A.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: If I had a car, I would drive you home.
My mom made me clean the bathroom.
I heard someone call my name outside.
I wonder whether the museum is open today.
Do you know where is the nearest subway station?
A.explain_ko: 간접의문문은 '의문사+주어+동사' 어순이므로 where the nearest subway station is가 되어야 한다.

A.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
A.passage:
a. This is the town where I was born.
b. Seeing from the sky, the island looks like a heart.
c. If I had left earlier, I would catch the train.
d. I don't know the way how he solved the puzzle.
e. Having finished his homework, he went out to play.
A.explain_ko: a·e가 맞다. b는 섬이 '보이는' 것이므로 Seen, c는 가정법 과거완료이므로 would have caught, d는 the way와 how를 함께 쓰지 않는다.

A.question: 다음 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
A.passage:
I met a chef (A) _____ restaurant is famous for fish soup.
We kept playing (B) _____ the heavy rain.
A.explain_ko: (A)는 '그의 식당'이므로 소유격 관계대명사 whose, (B)는 뒤에 명사구 the heavy rain이 오므로 전치사 despite.

A.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
The number of tourists visiting the old harbor have increased sharply.
She enjoys reading novels, painting landscapes, and hiking.
The fact that he lied surprised everyone in the room.
Little did she know that the test was canceled.
A.explain_ko: 주어의 중심은 The number(단수)이므로 have가 아니라 has. 나머지는 도치·병렬·동격 that이 바르다.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A.passage: It was not until the lights in the stadium went out _____ we realized how late it had become.
A.explain_ko: '~하고 나서야 비로소 …했다'는 It was not until ~ that … 강조 구문이므로 that. before·since·unless·then은 뜻으로 그럴듯하지만 이 구문에 쓸 수 없다.

A.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage: Before a game or a race, many players spend a few minutes warming up. They jog slowly, swing their arms, and stretch their legs. When your body is cold, your muscles are stiff, like a rubber band in a freezer. If you suddenly run fast, a stiff muscle can get hurt easily. Warming up makes your heart beat faster and sends more blood to your muscles. Then the muscles become warm and soft, so they move more freely. So next time you play a sport, don't skip those first few minutes. They help keep your body safe.
choices: how to become a faster runner
the best sports for staying healthy
the role of the heart in the body
ways to keep rubber bands soft
why warming up before exercise is important
A.explain_ko: 운동 전 준비 운동이 근육을 따뜻하고 부드럽게 해 부상을 막는다는 글. 심장·고무줄은 지문 낱말을 쓴 다른 초점의 오답.

A.question: washboard에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage:
Before washing machines, people washed clothes by hand. One useful tool for this was the washboard. It was a wooden frame with a board full of small ridges. First, people stood the board in a tub of soapy water. Then they rubbed wet clothes up and down on the ridges. This pushed the dirt out. Early washboards were made of wood, but later many were made of metal. Washing this way took a lot of time and hard work. Today, few people wash clothes with a washboard, but some musicians still play it as an instrument!
* ridge: 볼록 튀어나온 줄
choices: 판에 작은 줄이 많이 나 있었다.
A.explain_ko: 초기 빨래판은 나무로 만들었고 나중에 금속으로 만든 것이 많아졌다고 했으므로 '처음부터 금속'은 틀리다.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A.passage: On a cold morning, touch a metal spoon and a wooden spoon. The metal spoon feels much colder. But both spoons are actually the same temperature! They have been in the same room all night. So why do they feel different? Your hand is warmer than the spoons, so heat moves from your hand into them. Metal carries heat away from your skin very _____. Wood does this very slowly. Your skin feels the heat leaving, and your brain says, "This is cold!" That is why a metal door handle feels colder than a wooden one in winter.
A.explain_ko: 나무는 열을 천천히 옮긴다는 대조 문장이 뒤따르므로 금속은 열을 '빨리' 빼앗는다. slowly는 지문 낱말을 그대로 쓴 오답.

A.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage:
Have you ever seen a city bus lean toward the sidewalk at a stop? Many modern buses can "kneel." When the bus stops, the driver presses a button, and air is let out of the springs near the front wheels. This lowers the front door by several centimeters, so the first step becomes much closer to the curb. For a person in a wheelchair, an older passenger with weak knees, or a parent pushing a stroller, those few centimeters make a big difference. Some buses also have a ramp that slides out from the door. With these features, more people can travel on their own.
* curb: (인도 가장자리의) 연석
choices: Why City Buses Break Down So Often
Buses That Bend Down for Every Rider
How Bus Drivers Learn to Drive Safely
The Danger of Crowded Bus Stops
Wheelchairs: A Short History of Design
A.explain_ko: 버스가 앞쪽을 낮춰 휠체어 이용자·노인·유모차 승객이 쉽게 타게 한다는 글. 고장·휠체어 역사는 지문 낱말을 쓴 다른 초점.

A.question: Nora Ellis에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage: Nora Ellis is a furniture designer in the town of Pinecrest. She makes chairs and benches from broken skateboards. She started this work in 2019, when a local skate park threw away a pile of old boards. Nora liked their bright colors and strong wood, so she took them home. Most skateboards are made of seven thin layers of wood pressed together. When Nora cuts and sands a board, these layers appear like stripes. She never paints her chairs, because she wants people to see the boards' original colors. Last year, she held a free class for teenagers, and twelve students built their own stools.
choices: 보드를 자르고 다듬으면 나무 층이 줄무늬처럼 보인다.
작년에 십 대를 위한 무료 수업을 열었다.
A.explain_ko: 보드의 원래 색을 보여 주려고 의자에 절대 색칠하지 않는다고 했다.

A.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
A.passage: Many cooks soak dried beans in water before they cook them. ① Dried beans are hard because most of their water has been removed. ② When they sit in water overnight, they slowly drink it in and become larger and softer. ③ Beans have been grown by farmers around the world for thousands of years. ④ As a result, soaked beans cook faster and more evenly, and fewer of them split open in the pot. ⑤ Soaking also lets cooks pour away the water, along with some dust from the beans. So a little planning the night before can make a better meal the next day.
A.explain_ko: 마른 콩을 물에 불리는 까닭을 설명하는 글인데 ③은 콩 재배의 역사로 초점이 다르다.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage: Out in the open sea, a wave can travel a long way without breaking. But when it reaches a beach, it suddenly rises, curls over, and crashes into white foam. Why does this happen? A wave is not only on the surface; its movement reaches down into the water below. In deep water, nothing gets in its way. As the wave moves into shallow water near the shore, however, its lower part begins to drag along the sea floor. In other words, _____. The wave grows taller and steeper until it can no longer hold its shape, and the top falls forward. Surfers wait for this moment, because a breaking wave gives them the push they need.
choices: the whole wave moves faster toward the beach
the wave loses its height and quietly disappears
the top of the wave stops before the bottom does
the bottom of the wave slows down while the top keeps going
the sea floor pushes the wave back out to sea
A.explain_ko: 아랫부분이 바닥에 끌려 느려지는 동안 윗부분은 계속 나아가 파도가 높아지고 앞으로 쓰러진다. 위·아래를 뒤바꾼 것이 매력적 오답.

A.question: Goalball에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage: Goalball is a team sport made for athletes who are blind or have low vision. Two teams of three players face each other on an indoor court, with a wide goal at each end. Players take turns rolling a heavy ball across the floor toward the other team's goal. Defenders stop it by throwing their whole bodies down in its path. How do they know where the ball is? There are small bells inside the ball, so players follow it by sound. Because players rely on this sound, fans must stay silent while the ball is in play. Every player also wears eyeshades, so those with some sight have no advantage. Goalball is played at the Paralympic Games.
choices: 시력이 조금 남은 선수는 안대를 쓰지 않는다.
한 팀은 세 명의 선수로 이루어진다.
공을 바닥으로 굴려 상대편 골에 넣으려 한다.
공 안에 작은 방울이 들어 있다.
공이 움직이는 동안 관중은 조용히 해야 한다.
A.explain_ko: 모든 선수가 어두운 안대를 써서 시력이 남은 선수도 유리하지 않게 한다고 했다.

A.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
A.passage:
Before electric refrigerators became common, many families kept their food cold in an icebox. ( ① ) It was a wooden cabinet lined with metal, with a thick layer of cork or sawdust inside the walls to keep warm air out. ( ② ) A large block of ice was placed in a box near the top of the cabinet. ( ③ ) Of course, the ice slowly melted, so a worker called the iceman brought new blocks to homes several times a week. ( ④ ) Meanwhile, the melted water dripped into a pan under the icebox, and someone had to empty it every day. ( ⑤ ) If people forgot, the kitchen floor was soon covered with water, and the food on the shelves began to spoil.
* sawdust: 톱밥
A.given: Because cold air is heavier than warm air, it sank down and cooled the milk, butter, and meat on the shelves below.
A.explain_ko: 얼음을 맨 위 칸에 넣는다는 문장 뒤에, 그 찬 공기가 아래로 내려가 음식을 식힌다는 설명이 이어져야 한다.

A.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage: When people design a poster, a web page, or a book cover, they often feel that every empty corner must be filled. Yet experienced designers treat empty space as a material in its own right, just like color or type. This space, often called white space even when it is not white, gives the eye a place to rest. Without it, words and images compete for attention, and the viewer does not know where to look first. With enough of it, the most important element stands out naturally, because nothing nearby is fighting it. Empty space can also change how a design feels: a crowded layout may seem cheap or urgent, while a spacious one tends to look calm and confident. In short, what designers leave out matters as much as what they put in.
choices: the value of empty space in making designs effective
the history of using the color white in posters
ways to choose the right colors for a book cover
the need to fill every corner of a page with images
why viewers prefer crowded and urgent web pages
A.explain_ko: 빈 공간이 시선을 쉬게 하고 핵심을 돋보이게 하며 느낌을 바꾼다는 글. 흰색·색 고르기는 지문 낱말을 쓴 좁은 초점, 넷째·다섯째는 글과 반대.

A.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
A.passage: Water does not always boil at 100°C. The temperature at which it boils depends on the air pressure above it. ① High in the mountains, where the air pressure is lower, water boils at a lower temperature, so food takes longer to cook. ② Mountain villages are also popular with tourists who want clean air and beautiful views. ③ A pressure cooker does the opposite: by sealing the pot tightly, it traps steam and raises the pressure inside. ④ Under this higher pressure, water can reach about 120°C before boiling, so beans and tough meat become tender in a fraction of the usual time. ⑤ For example, a beef stew that simmers for three hours in an ordinary pot can be ready in about forty minutes. Understanding pressure, then, explains both slow cooking on mountaintops and fast cooking at home.
A.explain_ko: 기압과 끓는점의 관계로 고산 지대와 압력솥을 설명하는 글인데 ②는 산골 마을 관광 이야기로, 같은 '산'을 다루지만 초점이 다르다.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage: When a city road is always jammed, the obvious answer seems to be to build more lanes. For a short time, this often works: traffic flows faster, and drivers are pleased. Within a few years, however, the new road is frequently just as crowded as the old one. Transportation planners explain this pattern by pointing out that _____. When a trip becomes quicker, people who used to take the bus, travel at quieter hours, or simply stay home start driving at rush hour. New shops and apartments also appear along the wider road, adding even more trips. As a result, the extra lanes fill up again. For this reason, many cities now focus on improving buses and trains instead of only widening their roads.
choices: most drivers dislike roads with many lanes
wider roads are more expensive to repair
buses cause most of the traffic in cities
new lanes are usually built too slowly
more road space tends to attract more drivers
A.explain_ko: 길이 빨라지면 버스 이용자·다른 시간대 이용자까지 차를 몰고 나와 다시 막힌다는 내용이므로 '도로가 늘면 차도 는다'.

A.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage:
We usually think of microbes as enemies of food: they turn milk sour, make bread moldy, and spoil vegetables left too long in the fridge. Yet for thousands of years, people in nearly every culture have preserved food not by keeping microbes out but by deliberately inviting certain ones in. In fermentation, harmless bacteria or yeasts are given the conditions they prefer, such as salt, warmth, or the absence of air. As they multiply, they consume sugars and release acids or alcohol, creating an environment in which harmful organisms struggle to survive. Cabbage becomes kimchi, milk becomes yogurt, and soybeans become soy sauce, each lasting far longer than the raw ingredient would. Seen this way, fermentation is less a battle against decay than a carefully managed form of it, one in which humans decide which microbes win.
* microbe: 미생물
choices: Why Microbes Are Always the Enemy of Food
Kimchi and Yogurt: Popular Foods Around the World
Spoiling Food on Purpose to Keep It Safe
How the Refrigerator Changed the Way We Eat
The Health Benefits of Eating Fermented Food
A.explain_ko: 발효는 미생물을 막는 대신 이로운 미생물을 골라 들여 '관리된 부패'로 음식을 지키는 방법이라는 글. 둘째는 글과 반대, 셋째·다섯째는 범위가 좁거나 다른 초점.

A.question: the drift card study에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage: To learn how surface currents move along one stretch of coastline, researchers at the Calder Bay Marine Lab released 400 small wooden cards from a fishing boat about ten kilometers offshore. Each card was printed with a number and a short message asking the finder to report where and when it had been found. Over the following three months, members of the public reported 132 of the cards, roughly one in three. Surprisingly, most of these had washed up to the south of the release point, even though the main current in the area had long been believed to flow north. The researchers suspect that strong seasonal winds pushed the light cards in the opposite direction. They admit, however, that the results may be biased, since cards landing on remote or rocky shores were far less likely to be noticed and reported than those on popular beaches.
choices: 연구팀은 해안에서 약 10km 떨어진 배에서 카드를 띄웠다.
카드에는 발견한 장소와 때를 알려 달라는 글이 있었다.
석 달 동안 전체 카드의 약 3분의 1이 보고되었다.
보고된 카드의 대부분은 출발 지점의 북쪽에서 발견되었다.
외딴 해안에 닿은 카드는 보고될 가능성이 낮았다.
A.explain_ko: 대부분의 카드는 출발 지점의 남쪽에서 발견되어, 북쪽으로 흐른다고 믿어 온 해류와 반대였다.

A.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
A.passage:
For centuries, restoring a damaged painting usually meant making it look as if nothing had ever happened to it. ( ① ) Restorers freely repainted missing areas, sometimes adding details the original artist had never painted, and their work was often impossible to tell apart from the original. ( ② ) Today, most conservators reject this approach, since it quietly replaces the artist's own choices with someone else's guesses. ( ③ ) When a section of a painting has been lost entirely, they generally avoid inventing what might once have been there, however skillfully they could do so. ( ④ ) This way, the painting can still be enjoyed as a whole, while anyone who looks carefully can see exactly where the damage lies. ( ⑤ ) Equally important, modern conservators use materials that can later be removed without harming the original paint, so that future experts, armed with better knowledge, remain free to correct today's decisions.
* conservator: (미술품) 보존 전문가
A.given: Instead, they fill such gaps with a plain, neutral tone that blends in from a distance but is easy to spot up close.
A.explain_ko: 사라진 부분을 지어내 그리지 않는다는 문장 뒤에 Instead로 '대신 중간색으로 메운다'가 오고, 이어 This way가 그 효과를 말한다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 만나기로 한 장소를 고르시오.
A.explain_ko: 지하철역은 붐빈다며 정문 옆 매표소 앞에서 만나자고 했다. 정문은 매표소 위치를 설명하려고 나온 말.
A.script:
W: Jason, are you going to the basketball game on Saturday?
M: Yes. My dad got two tickets. Do you want to come with me?
W: Sure! Where should we meet? At the subway station?
M: It'll be too crowded there. Let's meet in front of the ticket office. It's easy to find. It's right next to the main gate.
W: Okay. See you there at five.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
A.explain_ko: 자전거 2대×2시간×6달러=24달러, 바구니 1개 1달러를 더해 25달러, 도서관 카드 할인 2달러를 빼면 23달러.
A.script:
M: Hi. We'd like to rent two bikes to ride along the river.
W: Sure. It's six dollars an hour for each bike.
M: We want to ride for two hours. Do you have helmets?
W: Yes. Helmets are free, but a basket costs one dollar per bike.
M: Then we'll take one basket for my bike. My sister doesn't need one.
W: All right. Oh, do you have a city library card? Card holders get two dollars off the total.
M: Yes, here it is.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, Old Tools Day에 관해 언급되지 __않은__ 것을 고르시오.
A.explain_ko: 버터 만들기·손재봉틀 체험, 5월 18일, 학생 무료·어른 3달러, 활동마다 20명은 나왔지만 주차는 나오지 않았다.
A.script:
W: Kevin, look at this poster. The Greenfield History Museum is having Old Tools Day.
M: Old Tools Day? What's that?
W: Visitors can try using things people used a hundred years ago, like a butter churn and a sewing machine you turn by hand.
M: Sounds fun. When is it?
W: It's on May 18th, from ten to four.
M: Do we have to pay?
W: It's free for students, but adults pay three dollars.
M: Great. Should we sign up first?
W: No, we can just go. But it says to arrive early because each activity has only twenty spots.

A.question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 수영장 공사로 인한 휴관 일정을 안내하려고
수영장 레인을 속도별로 나누어 운영한다는 것을 알리려고
A.explain_ko: 다음 주 월요일부터 여섯 레인을 느림·보통·빠름으로 나눠 쓴다는 안내다. 표지판 설치는 그 방식의 일부일 뿐 공사 휴관이 아니다.
A.script: M: Good evening, members. This is Daniel Brooks, manager of the Hillcrest Swimming Center. Starting next Monday, we will change the way our pool lanes are used. Until now, swimmers of all speeds have shared the same lanes, and many of you told us this caused crowding and even a few collisions. From now on, the six lanes will be divided by speed. Lanes one and two will be for slow swimmers, lanes three and four for medium swimmers, and lanes five and six for fast swimmers. Signs showing the speed of each lane will be placed at both ends of the pool. Please choose the lane that matches your pace. Thank you.

A.question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Megan이 Ryan에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: You should buy more seafood before you start cooking.
Let's just order dinner from a restaurant instead.
I'm sure Grandma will love a really spicy stew.
Why don't you use less chili and put some hot sauce on the table?
Could you cut the vegetables into smaller pieces?
A.explain_ko: 할머니가 매운 음식을 못 드시니 고추를 하나만 넣고 매운 소스를 따로 내자고 제안하려는 상황이다.
A.script: W: Ryan has offered to cook dinner for his family this weekend. He has found a recipe for a spicy seafood stew online and has already bought all the ingredients. While he is cutting the vegetables, his older sister, Megan, comes into the kitchen. She notices that the recipe calls for three fresh chili peppers, and she remembers that their grandmother, who is joining them for dinner, cannot eat very spicy food. However, Ryan is excited about making the dish exactly as the recipe says. Megan thinks he can still make a great stew if he uses only one pepper and puts some chili sauce on the table for those who want more heat. So she wants to suggest this idea to Ryan. In this situation, what would Megan most likely say to Ryan?

A.question: 우리말에 맞게 (use, keep, fresh)을 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 모양을 바꾸세요.
A.hint_ko: 우리는 음식을 신선하게 유지하기 위해 소금을 사용한다.
A.explain_ko: '~하기 위해'는 to+동사원형. keep+목적어+형용사로 '~을 …하게 유지하다'.

A.question: 우리말에 맞게 (boat, make)을 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 모양을 바꾸세요.
A.hint_ko: 이 배는 나의 할아버지에 의해 만들어졌다.
A.explain_ko: 과거 수동태는 was+과거분사(made), 행위자는 by+목적격.

A.question: 우리말에 맞게 (know, when, leave)을 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 모양을 바꾸세요.
A.explain_ko: 간접의문문은 '의문사+주어+동사' 어순. 주어 the next train이 3인칭 단수라 leaves.

A.question: 우리말에 맞게 (know, win)을 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 모양을 바꾸세요.
A.hint_ko: 내가 규칙을 알았더라면, 나는 이겼을 텐데.
A.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대는 If+주어+had p.p., 주어+would have p.p.

A.question: 우리말에 맞게 (little, know, close)을 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 모양을 바꾸세요.
A.hint_ko: 나는 그 가게가 이미 문을 닫아 버렸다는 것을 전혀 몰랐다.
A.explain_ko: 부정어 Little이 문장 앞에 오면 'did+주어+동사원형'으로 도치. 9칸이므로 접속사 that을 쓴다. had closed와 was closed 모두 정답.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __arrive__
B.explain_ko: arrive는 '도착하다'. 출발하다=leave/depart, 기다리다=wait.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __dangerous__
B.explain_ko: dangerous는 '위험한'. 안전한=safe, 중요한=important.

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __나뭇잎__
B.explain_ko: 나뭇잎은 leaf. leap(뛰다)·lead(이끌다)는 철자가 비슷한 다른 낱말.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __shade__
B.explain_ko: shade는 '그늘'. 가지=branch, 뿌리=root.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __rare__
B.explain_ko: rare는 '드문, 희귀한'. 흔한=common, 거친=rough.

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __발명하다__
B.explain_ko: 발명하다는 invent. invite(초대하다)·involve(포함하다)는 같은 in-으로 시작하는 다른 동사.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __recover__
B.explain_ko: recover는 '회복하다'. 거절하다=refuse, 기억하다=remember.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __fuel__
B.explain_ko: fuel은 '연료'. 재료=material, 연기=smoke.

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __정확한__
B.explain_ko: 정확한은 accurate. adequate(충분한)·accustomed(익숙한)는 ac-/ad-로 시작하는 비슷한 형용사.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __evaporate__
B.explain_ko: evaporate는 '증발하다'. 응결하다=condense, 얼다=freeze.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __fragile__
B.explain_ko: fragile은 '깨지기 쉬운, 연약한'. 유연한=flexible, 단단한=solid.

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __생존__
B.explain_ko: 생존은 survival. revival(부활)·arrival(도착)은 -val로 끝나는 비슷한 명사.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __inevitable__
B.explain_ko: inevitable은 '피할 수 없는, 필연적인'. 되돌릴 수 없는=irreversible, 예측할 수 없는=unpredictable.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __deteriorate__
B.explain_ko: deteriorate는 '악화되다, 나빠지다'. 개선되다=improve, 회복되다=recover로 반대 방향.

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __지속 가능성__
B.explain_ko: 지속 가능성은 sustainability. suitability(적합성)·susceptibility(민감성)는 su-로 시작하고 -ability로 끝나는 비슷한 명사.

B.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
B.passage: How _____ sugar do you put in your tea?
B.explain_ko: sugar는 셀 수 없는 명사라 How much를 쓴다. many·a few·few는 셀 수 있는 명사 앞, lots는 How 뒤에 올 수 없다.

B.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: Don't touch the flowers in the garden.
He washes his hands before every meal.
Be careful when you cross the street.
Our teacher doesn't drink coffee in the morning.
My sister can plays the violin very well.
B.explain_ko: 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 plays → play. 나머지는 부정 명령문, 3인칭 단수 -es, be 명령문, doesn't+원형으로 맞다.

B.question: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?
B.passage: Ella gave up (A) _____ sweets last month. Now she plans (B) _____ more fruit and vegetables.
B.explain_ko: give up은 동명사를 목적어로(eating), plan은 to부정사를 목적어로(to eat) 쓴다.

B.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
B.passage:
a. This soup smells wonderful.
b. I have visited the museum last Sunday.
c. The window was broken by the strong wind.
d. Your idea sounds greatly.
e. She has lived in this town since 2020.
B.explain_ko: a·c·e가 맞다(3개). b는 last Sunday 같은 과거 시점과 현재완료를 함께 쓸 수 없고, d는 감각동사 sound 뒤에 부사가 아닌 형용사 great가 와야 한다.

B.question: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?
B.passage: This bike is (A) _____ I wanted for my birthday. The boy (B) _____ next to Jane is my cousin.
B.explain_ko: (A) 선행사가 없으므로 '~하는 것'의 what. (B) 명사 The boy를 꾸미는 현재분사 sitting. that·which는 선행사가 필요하고, sat·sits는 수식어 자리에 올 수 없다.

B.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: If I had a car, I would drive you home.
My mom made me clean the bathroom.
I heard someone call my name outside.
I wonder whether she will join us.
Can you tell me where is the bus stop?
B.explain_ko: 간접의문문은 '의문사+주어+동사' 순서이므로 where the bus stop is가 맞다. 나머지는 가정법 과거, 사역동사·지각동사+원형, whether 간접의문문으로 맞다.

B.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
B.passage:
a. This is the park where I first met my best friend.
b. Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
c. If she had studied harder, she would pass the exam last year.
d. I still remember the day which we moved into this house.
e. Written in a hurry, he made many mistakes in the letter.
B.explain_ko: a·b만 맞다(2개). c는 과거 사실의 반대이므로 would have passed, d는 시간 선행사 뒤 관계부사 when(on which), e는 주어 he가 쓴 것이므로 Writing이 되어야 한다.

B.question: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?
B.passage: I met a woman (A) _____ son plays the cello in the city orchestra. (B) _____ the heavy rain, the outdoor concert went on as planned.
B.explain_ko: (A) 뒤에 명사 son이 바로 오므로 소유격 관계대명사 whose. (B) 뒤에 명사구 the heavy rain이 오므로 전치사 Despite. Although·Though는 절을 이끄는 접속사.

B.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: Only after the storm passed did we leave the shelter.
She enjoys reading novels and writing short poems.
The news that the river was cleaned surprised everyone.
The number of students who walk to school have increased.
Each of the workers has a different role in the project.
B.explain_ko: 주어의 핵심은 The number(단수)이므로 have → has. 나머지는 Only 부사구 도치, 동명사 병렬, 동격 that, Each of+복수명사의 단수 동사로 맞다.

B.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
B.passage: Jake had his umbrella when he got on the bus, but he did not have it when he walked into class. He _____ it somewhere on the bus.
B.explain_ko: 버스를 탈 때는 있었고 교실에서는 없었으므로 과거 일에 대한 강한 확신(must have p.p.) must have left. should have left는 '두고 왔어야 했다'(후회), cannot have left는 근거와 반대, must leave는 현재·미래 의무, need not have left는 '두고 올 필요가 없었는데'로 뜻이 맞지 않는다.

B.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage:
Have you ever touched the soft green carpet on a rock or a tree in the forest? That is moss. Moss is a very small plant. It has no flowers and no seeds. Instead of roots, it has tiny hairs that hold on to rocks and wood. Moss is small, but it does important work. It drinks rain like a sponge and keeps the forest floor wet. Small insects and spiders live in it. Moss also slowly breaks rocks into soil, so other plants can grow there later. Next time, look down and thank the moss.
* moss: 이끼
choices: how to grow moss at home
why moss has no flowers or seeds
small insects that live in moss
the important roles of moss in a forest
the ways rain helps forest trees grow
B.explain_ko: 이끼가 숲에서 물을 머금고, 작은 생물의 집이 되고, 흙을 만드는 역할을 설명한다. 꽃·씨가 없다는 것과 곤충 이야기는 일부 내용, 기르는 법·비의 역할은 다른 초점.

B.question: Maple Street Repair Café에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage: Do you have a broken lamp or a toaster that doesn't work? Don't throw it away! Bring it to the Maple Street Repair Café. It opens on the first Saturday of every month, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at the community center. Volunteers there fix clothes, toys, bikes, and small machines for free. You can watch them and learn how to fix things yourself. While you wait, you can enjoy free tea and cookies. Last year, the volunteers fixed more than 600 items. Please bring only one item each time, and nothing bigger than a chair.
choices: 매달 첫째 토요일에 주민 센터에서 열린다.
한 번에 물건을 두 개까지 가져올 수 있다.
고치는 모습을 보며 고치는 법을 배울 수 있다.
B.explain_ko: 마지막 문장에서 한 번에 한 개만 가져오라고 했다. 나머지는 지문 내용과 일치한다.

B.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage:
During a storm, you first see a flash of lightning. A few seconds later, you hear the loud sound of thunder. But they actually happen at the same time. Why do we see lightning first? It is because light travels much _____ than sound. Light reaches your eyes almost at once, but sound needs about three seconds to travel one kilometer. So you can find out how far away a storm is. Count the seconds between the flash and the thunder, and divide the number by three. If you count six seconds, the storm is about two kilometers away.
* lightning: 번개
B.explain_ko: 빛은 거의 바로 오고 소리는 1km에 약 3초가 걸리므로 빛이 소리보다 훨씬 '빠르다'. slower는 반대, louder·lower는 소리 성질, later는 의미가 맞지 않는다.

B.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage:
When you feel cold or watch a scary movie, small bumps sometimes appear on your arms. These are called goosebumps. Each bump forms when a tiny muscle at the bottom of a hair pulls tight and makes the hair stand up. For people today, this does not do much, because our body hair is thin. But for our hairy ancestors and for many animals, it was very useful. When their hair stood up, it trapped warm air close to the skin. It also made them look bigger to their enemies. A cat with its fur standing up is a good example. Goosebumps are a small reminder of our past.
* ancestor: 조상
choices: How to Stay Warm on Cold Days
Why Scary Movies Make Us Feel Cold
The Tiny Muscles That Move Our Arms
Goosebumps: A Gift from Our Furry Past
B.explain_ko: 소름이 털이 많던 조상에게 쓸모 있던 반응의 흔적이라는 글. 추위·무서운 영화·근육·고양이는 지문 낱말을 쓴 좁거나 다른 초점의 오답.

B.question: Daniel Reyes에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage:
Daniel Reyes has a job that few people know about. He is a smokejumper. Smokejumpers are firefighters who jump out of airplanes to fight wildfires in faraway forests. Some forest fires start in places with no roads, so fire trucks cannot reach them. Then smokejumpers parachute down near the fire and dig lines in the ground to stop it from spreading. Daniel carries about 50 kilograms of tools and food, and he often works for two or three days without a bed. Before his first jump, he trained for eight weeks. "The work is hard," he says, "but saving a forest makes me proud."
* wildfire: 산불
choices: 첫 점프 전에 4주 동안 훈련을 받았다.
비행기에서 뛰어내려 산불을 끄는 일을 한다.
땅에 선을 파서 불이 번지는 것을 막는다.
일이 힘들지만 숲을 구하는 것이 자랑스럽다고 말한다.
B.explain_ko: 첫 점프 전 훈련 기간은 8주(eight weeks)였다. 숫자를 바꾼 선택지가 답이고 나머지는 지문과 일치한다.

B.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
B.passage:
Braille is a writing system that lets people who cannot see read with their fingers. ① Each letter is made of raised dots placed in a small box with six spaces. ② By touching different patterns of dots, readers can tell one letter from another. ③ Louis Braille, a French boy who lost his sight as a child, created this system when he was only about fifteen years old. ④ Guide dogs need about two years of training before they can work with a blind person. ⑤ Today, Braille is used not only in books but also on elevator buttons, medicine boxes, and signs in public buildings.
* raised: 도드라진, 튀어나온
B.explain_ko: 점자의 구조·만든 사람·쓰임을 설명하는 글인데 ④는 시각 장애인을 돕는 안내견 훈련 이야기로 초점이 다르다.

B.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage:
When astronauts return from a long stay in space, they are often a little taller than before. Some grow as much as five centimeters. How does this happen? Our spine is made of small bones with soft pads between them. On Earth, gravity always pulls down on our bodies, so these pads are pressed together all day. In space, however, there is almost no gravity to push them down. As a result, the pads spread out, and the spine gets longer. This change does not last, though. Soon after astronauts come back to Earth, gravity presses the pads together again, and they return to their usual height. In other words, astronauts stay taller only _____.
* spine: 척추
choices: because their bones grow longer in space
when they eat special food in space
after they come back to Earth
while gravity is not pressing on their spines
if they exercise hard every day
B.explain_ko: 뼈 사이 패드를 누르는 중력이 없을 때만 척추가 늘어나므로 '중력이 척추를 누르지 않는 동안'만 키가 크다. 뼈가 자란다·지구로 돌아온 뒤는 지문과 반대, 음식·운동은 근거 없는 이유.

B.question: Brookfield's food waste program에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage:
Last spring, the town of Brookfield started a new program to reduce food waste. Every family received a small green bin for kitchen scraps such as fruit peels, eggshells, and coffee grounds. Each Tuesday, trucks collect the bins and take the scraps to a large composting center outside the town. There, the scraps are mixed with dry leaves and slowly turn into rich soil over about three months. The soil is then given back to residents for free, so they can use it in their gardens. However, meat and bones are not allowed in the bins because they attract wild animals. In its first year, the program kept about 900 tons of food out of the landfill.
* scrap: 찌꺼기
* composting: 퇴비 만들기
* landfill: 쓰레기 매립지
choices: 과일 껍질과 달걀 껍데기 같은 음식 찌꺼기를 모은다.
고기와 뼈도 초록색 통에 넣을 수 있다.
음식 찌꺼기는 약 석 달에 걸쳐 흙으로 바뀐다.
만들어진 흙은 주민들에게 무료로 나누어 준다.
B.explain_ko: 고기와 뼈는 야생 동물을 끌어들여 통에 넣을 수 없다고 했다. 나머지는 지문 순서대로 일치한다.

B.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
B.passage:
For most living things, a forest fire means danger. ( ① ) Some pine trees, however, actually need fire to spread their seeds. ( ② ) Their cones are sealed shut with a thick, sticky substance called resin, and they can stay closed on the branches for many years. ( ③ ) When a fire passes through the forest, its great heat melts the resin, and the cones finally open. ( ④ ) The seeds then fall onto ground that has just been cleared by the fire. ( ⑤ ) With plenty of sunlight and ash full of nutrients, the young trees can grow quickly. There is little competition from other plants, too. In this way, the end of an old forest becomes the beginning of a new one.
* cone: 솔방울
* resin: 송진
B.given: Even the strong sunshine of a hot summer day is not enough to open them.
B.explain_ko: 주어진 문장의 them은 오랫동안 닫혀 있는 솔방울(cones)을 가리키고, 햇빛으로는 안 열린다는 내용이 '불의 열이 송진을 녹여 열린다'는 문장 바로 앞(③)에 와야 대조가 자연스럽다.

B.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage:
Long before machines did heavy work, people relied on songs to get difficult jobs done. Workers pulling heavy ropes, cutting grain, or pounding rice often sang together as they moved. These work songs were not simply a way to pass the time. Their steady beat told everyone exactly when to pull, lift, or swing, so that a whole group could act as one body. Usually, a leader sang a line, and the others answered, timing their effort to the rhythm. Without such signals, workers might pull at different moments and waste their strength, or even injure one another with their tools. The songs also helped people ignore their tiredness and forget the dull repetition of the task. In this sense, music was once as practical a tool as a hammer or a rope.
* pound: 빻다, 찧다
choices: the history of machines replacing human workers
the practical role of songs in coordinating group labor
the ways leaders chose songs for their workers
how singing at work improves people's voices
the dangers of using heavy tools without training
B.explain_ko: 노동요의 박자가 여럿의 움직임을 맞추고 피로를 잊게 한 실용적 기능이 주제. 기계의 역사·도구의 위험은 지문 낱말을 쓴 다른 초점, 리더의 노래 선택·목소리 향상은 언급되지 않았다.

B.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
B.passage:
Most people think of a fever as something bad that must be stopped right away. In many cases, however, a fever is part of the body's defense system. ① When harmful germs enter the body, the brain raises its temperature on purpose, much like someone turning up a heater. ② Many bacteria and viruses multiply best at normal body temperature, so a few extra degrees can slow them down. ③ The first thermometers were large glass tubes that took many minutes to give a reading. ④ At the same time, a higher temperature helps certain white blood cells move faster and attack invaders more effectively. ⑤ This is why some doctors say that a mild fever in an otherwise healthy adult does not always need medicine. Of course, a very high fever can be dangerous, so it should still be checked by a doctor.
* multiply: 번식하다, 늘어나다
B.explain_ko: 열이 세균을 늦추고 면역 세포를 돕는 방어 작용이라는 흐름인데 ③은 체온계의 역사로 같은 소재(체온)의 다른 이야기다.

B.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: Of the roughly 7,000 languages spoken today, many are used only by a small group of elderly speakers. When such a language disappears, we lose more than a set of words and grammar rules. Many small languages hold detailed knowledge about the local environment. A community living in a rainforest, for example, may have dozens of separate names for plants that outsiders would simply call "trees" or "weeds." Each name might carry information about which leaves can heal a wound, which roots are poisonous, or which fruits ripen after the first rain. This knowledge is rarely written down; instead, it is passed from parents to children through everyday talk. Therefore, when the last speakers of a language are gone, _____ often vanishes with them.
choices: the need for a written alphabet
a library of knowledge about nature
the community's interest in modern medicine
a list of words that outsiders invented
B.explain_ko: 작은 언어의 식물 이름 하나하나에 자연에 대한 지식이 담겨 말로만 전해지므로, 언어가 사라지면 '자연에 관한 지식의 도서관'도 사라진다. 문법·문자·현대 의학은 지문 낱말을 빌린 엉뚱한 초점.

B.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: Most people assume that a job is something fixed: a list of duties written by an employer and accepted by a worker. Yet those who study the workplace have noticed that many employees quietly reshape their jobs from within. A bus driver, for instance, may come to see his role not merely as moving people from stop to stop but as caring for a neighborhood, so he learns the names of regular passengers and points out local events to visitors. A library assistant who loves games might start a weekly puzzle club. None of these changes appear in an official job description, yet they alter how the work feels. By adjusting their tasks, their relationships, and the way they think about their work, employees can turn the same position into something far more meaningful. In this sense, people do not simply fill jobs; they partly design them.
choices: Why Bus Drivers Need Better Training
How Employers Write Clear Job Descriptions
Rewriting Your Job from the Inside
Should Workers Change Jobs More Often?
The Rising Demand for Library Workers
B.explain_ko: 직원이 업무·관계·생각을 스스로 바꿔 같은 일을 더 의미 있게 만든다는 글이므로 '안에서부터 일을 다시 쓰기'. 버스 기사·도서관은 예시일 뿐이고, 직무 기술서·이직은 다른 초점.

B.question: the Northvale University study에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage:
Researchers at Northvale University recently examined whether showing families their electricity use in real time would lead them to save energy. They installed small screens in 240 homes; half of the screens displayed the household's current power use, while the other half showed nothing but the time. During the first month, homes with the energy displays used about 12 percent less electricity than the other group. However, the gap gradually narrowed, and by the fourth month it had almost disappeared, suggesting that the novelty of the screens had worn off. Interestingly, one subgroup kept saving: families whose screens also compared their use with that of similar households nearby. The researchers concluded that information alone rarely changes behavior for long, whereas information combined with a social comparison may have a more lasting effect on how people use energy at home.
* novelty: 새로움
choices: 첫 달에 화면이 있는 가정은 전기를 약 20퍼센트 덜 썼다.
넷째 달에는 두 집단의 차이가 거의 사라졌다.
이웃과의 비교를 함께 본 가정은 계속 절약했다.
B.explain_ko: 첫 달 절약 폭은 약 12퍼센트였다. 수치를 바꾼 선택지가 답이고 나머지는 지문 순서대로 일치한다.

B.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
B.passage:
Since the first satellite was launched in 1957, humans have sent thousands of objects into orbit around Earth. ( ① ) Many of them no longer work, yet they remain up there, circling the planet at tremendous speeds alongside used rocket parts, flecks of paint, and fragments from past explosions. ( ② ) Because this debris travels at nearly eight kilometers per second, even a piece the size of a coin can strike a working satellite harder than a bullet. ( ③ ) Instead, the crash scatters thousands of new pieces, each of which raises the chance of further collisions. ( ④ ) If such a chain reaction continued unchecked, certain orbits could become too dangerous to use for generations. ( ⑤ ) For this reason, several space agencies are now testing ways to capture dead satellites or guide them down into the atmosphere, where they burn up harmlessly. Keeping space clean, it seems, has become as important as exploring it.
* debris: 잔해, 파편
* fleck: 작은 조각
B.given: What worries scientists most, however, is that a single collision rarely ends with the loss of just two objects.
B.explain_ko: ③ 뒤의 Instead는 '충돌이 두 물체를 잃는 것으로 끝나지 않는다'는 부정 진술을 받아야 하므로 주어진 문장은 ③. 그 뒤의 such a chain reaction도 이 연결을 확인해 준다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 대화 직후에 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Jake, it's time to leave for school.
M: Okay, Mom. It's sunny now, so I'll just wear my cap.
W: Wait. The weather report says it will rain heavily this afternoon.
M: Really? But my umbrella is broken.
W: Then take your raincoat. It's in your closet.
M: Okay. I'll go and get it right now.
B.explain_ko: 우산이 고장 나서 엄마가 옷장의 우비를 챙기라고 하자 지금 가져오겠다고 했다. 모자·우산·일기 예보는 대화에 나온 낱말을 쓴 오답.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Welcome to Melody Music. How can I help you?
W: Hi. I need new strings for my guitar. How much are they?
M: This set is 12 dollars, and that one is 20 dollars.
W: I'll take the 12-dollar set. Do you sell guitar picks, too?
M: Yes. They're 1 dollar each, or 5 dollars for a pack of six.
W: Then I'll buy one pack, please.
M: Sure. Do you have a member card? Members get 10 percent off.
W: No, I don't.
M: That's okay. Let me ring these up for you.
B.explain_ko: 12달러 줄 세트 + 5달러 피크 한 묶음 = 17달러. 회원 카드가 없어 10퍼센트 할인을 받지 못한다($15.30은 할인 적용 시).

B.question: 대화를 듣고, Green Hill Tree Planting Day에 관해 언급되지 __않은__ 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Ryan, did you see the poster about the Green Hill Tree Planting Day?
M: No, I didn't. What is it?
W: Volunteers will plant 300 young trees along the river near Green Hill Park.
M: Sounds great. When is it?
W: It's on Saturday, April 12th, from 9 a.m. to noon.
M: Do we need to bring anything?
W: Just gloves and a water bottle. They'll give us shovels and the young trees.
M: Can anyone join?
W: Anyone over twelve can join, but you have to sign up online by this Wednesday.
M: Okay, let's sign up together right now.
B.explain_ko: 나무 300그루, 4월 12일 토요일, 장갑과 물병, 12세 이상은 언급되었지만 참가비는 나오지 않는다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Josh, you've been sitting at your desk for almost three hours.
M: I know. I'm trying to finish this report. Actually, I'm thinking about buying a standing desk.
W: A standing desk? Why?
M: I read that sitting all day is bad for your health.
W: That's true, but standing in one place for hours isn't great either. It can hurt your legs and lower back.
M: Really? Then what should I do?
W: I think the key is to move often. Just get up every thirty minutes and walk around or stretch for a couple of minutes.
M: That sounds easy enough.
W: It is. Short movement breaks keep your blood flowing, and they even help you focus better when you sit back down.
M: Okay. I'll set a timer on my phone.
choices: 서서 일하는 책상을 쓰면 건강에 도움이 된다.
보고서는 집중이 잘되는 아침에 쓰는 것이 좋다.
오래 앉아 있을 때는 자주 일어나 몸을 움직이는 것이 좋다.
허리가 아프면 바로 병원에 가야 한다.
휴대 전화 사용 시간을 줄여야 한다.
B.explain_ko: 여자는 서서 일하는 책상보다 30분마다 일어나 움직이는 짧은 휴식이 중요하다고 말한다. 서서 일하는 책상은 남자의 생각이고, 허리·휴대 전화는 대화 낱말을 쓴 오답.

B.question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Olivia가 Ben에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script: W: Ben and Olivia are members of a language exchange club. This week, Ben has to give a short talk in English about his favorite hobby, so he asks Olivia to listen to him practice. As he speaks, Olivia notices that his talk is full of long, difficult words that he found in a dictionary. Ben believes these words will make him sound smart. However, Olivia knows that most club members are beginners, and she is worried that they will not understand him. In her opinion, clear and simple words would help him share his ideas much better. So she wants to suggest that Ben replace the difficult words with easier ones. In this situation, what would Olivia most likely say to Ben?
choices: You should look up more words in the dictionary.
I think your talk is too short for the club meeting.
How about choosing a different hobby to talk about?
Why don't you use simpler words so everyone can follow you?
Speaking more slowly will make you sound smarter.
B.explain_ko: 초보 회원들이 이해하도록 어려운 낱말을 쉬운 말로 바꾸라고 제안하는 말이 알맞다. 사전·발표 길이·주제 바꾸기·말 속도는 상황과 맞지 않는다.

B.question: 우리말에 맞게 (to, see, outside)을(를) 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 형태를 바꾸세요.
B.hint_ko: 나는 별을 보기 위해 밖으로 나갔다.
B.explain_ko: '~하기 위해'는 to+동사원형: I went outside to see the stars.

B.question: 우리말에 맞게 (write)을(를) 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 형태를 바꾸세요.
B.hint_ko: 이 편지는 우리 할머니에 의해 쓰였다.
B.explain_ko: 과거 수동태는 was+과거분사(written)+by: This letter was written by my grandmother.

B.question: 우리말에 맞게 (tell, when)을(를) 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 형태를 바꾸세요.
B.hint_ko: 그 콘서트가 언제 시작하는지 나에게 말해 줄 수 있니?
B.explain_ko: 간접의문문은 '의문사+주어+동사' 순서: when the concert starts. 3인칭 단수 현재라 starts.

B.question: 우리말에 맞게 (know, call)을(를) 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 형태를 바꾸세요.
B.hint_ko: 내가 그 소식을 알았더라면, 너에게 전화했을 텐데.
B.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대는 If+주어+had p.p., 주어+would have p.p.: If I had known the news, I would have called you.

B.question: 우리말에 맞게 Never로 시작하여 (see, such)을(를) 써서 문장을 완성하세요. 필요하면 낱말의 형태를 바꾸세요.
B.hint_ko: 나는 지금까지 그렇게 밝은 오로라를 한 번도 본 적이 없다.
B.explain_ko: 부정어 Never를 문장 앞에 두면 '조동사+주어' 순서로 도치: Never have I seen such a bright aurora. I have never seen …은 도치가 아니다.
